subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wright <emma.wright@acmecorp.com>, Ben Taylor <ben.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Emma / Ben —

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the context on your product roadmap and the volume profile. Below is a short recap so we’re aligned and a suggested set of next steps.

TL;DR: primary ask is to get inference costs under control while keeping ~200ms P95 latency for end-user responses. We can run a short pilot to demonstrate ~40-60% unit-cost reduction using batching, caching, and a mixed-model routing approach.

Pain points you called out:
- High and unpredictable inference spend driven by chat volume (peak bursts during launches).
- Tight latency requirement: ~200ms P95 for user-facing chat.
- Large context windows for user history and retrieval results (average request ~1,800 tokens).
- Limited procurement budget this fiscal year — need clear ROI to justify changes.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce monthly inference spend to <= $200k (current baseline unclear — need final numbers).
- Maintain user experience latency target (<= 200ms P95).
- Pilot in a single product slice and measure cost / quality tradeoffs.

Quick TCO notes (high-level, ballpark):
- Your stated volume: ~1.2B tokens/month (we used this as demo baseline).
- Current vendor cost (example): $0.00040 / token -> ~$480k / month.
- Estimated with Redwood levers (batching + prefix/KV caching + 4-bit quantization + routing to cheaper model variants): effective unit cost ~ $0.00015 / token -> ~$180k / month (approx. 62% reduction on unit cost).
- Additional saving with Reserved/Dedicated capacity and committed discounts possible for consistent load.

Primary levers we’ll test in the pilot:
1) Smart batching & adaptive batching windows to increase throughput on steady-state traffic.
2) Prefix & KV caching for repeated prompts and retrieval results (reduces repeated attention computation).
3) Model routing: use a cheaper, verified model for common query types and route complex queries to higher-capacity models.
4) Quantization (4-bit/8-bit) for non-critical high-volume endpoints.

Requested next steps:
- I’ll share a TCO workbook (attached) with a worksheet you can update with your exact token counts so we can produce a tailored estimate.
- Can we get a heads-up on the procurement contact + any timing constraints for FY26 spend?
- Proposed follow-up: 30-45 minute pilot kickoff next week to align scope and success criteria.

Attachments: ACME_TCO_workbook_v2.xlsx (TCO workbook), redwood-pricing-deck.pdf

If that matches your view, I’ll schedule the pilot and loop in engineering for integration details.

Thanks —
Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Emma Wright <emma.wright@acmecorp.com>

Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we run numbers: 

1) Baseline confirmation: our telemetry shows ~1.05B tokens/mo across all chat endpoints (not 1.2B). Can you rerun the workbook against 1.05B?
2) Budget: procurement gave us a hard cap of $200k/year for inference for this product line for FY27 (yes, it’s tight). That’s why we need a clear plan that proves >70% reduction or a clear pathway to that with reserved commitments.
3) Latency: 200ms P95 is a hard requirement for the primary chat flow. We can accept slightly higher latency for background generators.

We’re happy to run a 6-8 week pilot if the savings look promising. Procurement is: procurement@acmecorp.com — loop them in for contracting.

Can you (a) update the workbook for 1.05B tokens and (b) provide a simple two-line ROI summary we can share with procurement?

Best,
Emma
Emma Wright
Head of Product — Conversational AI
Acme Corp

Emma — thanks for the quick reply and the procurement contact. I updated the attached workbook for 1.05B tokens and included two ROI summary options you can share:

ROI summary (two-line bullets for procurement):
- Baseline (1.05B tokens/mo at $0.00040/token): ~$420k/month -> ~$5.0M/year.
- Pilot projection (batching + caching + quantization + routing): ~$0.00012/token effective -> ~$126k/month -> ~$1.5M/year (approx. 70% reduction); additional savings available with reserved commitments.

Notes / assumptions:
- The projected unit cost assumes achieving ~45-60% cache hit on repeated prefixes and a 1.5-2.0x effective batching improvement on steady traffic. Results vary by prompt distribution; we’ll instrument to report token counts, cache hit rate, and latency.
- Latency: our target in-pilot SLO is 200ms P95 on the primary flow. Engineering will measure end-to-end (edge -> model). If routing to cheaper model variants introduces higher tail latency for a subset of queries, we’ll fallback to the primary model for those requests.

Attachments: ACME_TCO_workbook_v2.xlsx (updated for 1.05B), redwood-pricing-deck.pdf

Proposed pilot scope & timeline:
- Week 0: Kickoff + access to telemetry / sample prompts (2-3 days).
- Weeks 1-2: Instrumentation + baseline run (token-level telemetry).
- Weeks 3-6: Implement caching/batching/quantization toggles and run controlled A/B.
- Week 7: Review results + next-step decision (scale vs. purchase).

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and bring engineering.

Cheers,
Rafael
